title: Off-Diagonal Symmetry: Completing Newton-Girard
content:
The parent proof established (Σxᵢ)² = Σxᵢ² + Σ_{i≠j} xᵢxⱼ (diagonal/off-diagonal split). This file proves the final piece: Σ_{i≠j} xᵢxⱼ = 2·Σ_{i<j} xᵢxⱼ.

The proof pairs each off-diagonal entry (i,j) with its transpose (j,i). By symmetry of multiplication (xᵢxⱼ = xⱼxᵢ), both contribute equally, so the off-diagonal sum double-counts each ordered pair i < j.

The result is proved in full generality: for any symmetric function f(i,j) = f(j,i) over a linearly ordered finite set with values in any commutative ring.
mathContext: For $f(i,j) = f(j,i)$: $\sum_{i \neq j} f(i,j) = 2 \sum_{i < j} f(i,j)$. Applied to $f(i,j) = x_i x_j$: $\sum_{i \neq j} x_i x_j = 2 e_2$.

title: Main Theorem: Σ_{i≠j} f = 2·Σ_{i<j} f
content:
The main result combines three ingredients:

1. **Decomposition**: offDiag = upper ∪ lower (disjoint)
2. **Symmetry**: Σ_lower f = Σ_upper f (via Prod.swap bijection + f symmetry)
3. **Algebra**: Σ_upper + Σ_lower = Σ_upper + Σ_upper = 2·Σ_upper

The symmetry step (2) is the heart of the proof: rewrite each f(a,b) = f(b,a) = f(swap(a,b)), then use Finset.sum_image to reindex the lower-triangular sum as an upper-triangular sum.
